answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving, so spinning up fake identities costs real capital instead of being free. New agents start in a low-trust meadow where they can only take small jobs, earning their way toward a trusted haven only after a track record of honest work. An onyx ledger of signed attestations makes that history portable and hard to forge, so a discarded identity loses its earned reputation and must pay the entry cost again.
